newsitem.title: INDONESIA: E Timorese briefly protest in second town.
newsitem.headline: E Timorese briefly protest in second town.

text.p: About 300 people protested in East Timor's second largest town Baucau on Thursday in support of the territory's Noble laureate Bishop Carlos Belo as more than 5,000 others took to the streets in the capital Dili.

Colonel Atok Rismanto, deputy police chief in East Timor, told Reuters by telephone from Dili that the protest in Baucau, 100 km (60 miles) east of the capital, started about 9.00 a.m. (0100 GMT) and lasted three and half hours.
"In Baucau around 300 people had a demonstration which was orderly. There was no one arrested," Rismanto said.
Independent confirmation of the protest from Baucau was not immediately available.

The Portuguese news agency Lusa reported on Thursday that "hundreds of demonstrators" were detained in Baucau, Viqueque, on the southern coast and Laleia west of Baucau after trying to travel to Dili to join the protest there.
Rismanto said he did not have reports of protests in other districts except for Dili and Baucau.
"If the the Portuguese news agency says there were people arrested, it is misleading," he said.

There have been demonstrations in Dili three days running in support of Belo, who was born in the Baucau district, after protests and attacks in the media against the churchman for his reported comments that Indonesia treated Timorese like "dogs".
Belo, in Jakarta for a church meeting, has declined to comment on the report.

East Timor is a former Portuguese colony invaded by Indonesia in 1975 and declared its 27th province the following year in an act not recognised by the United Nations which regards Lisbon as being the administering power.
